@@ -68,6 +68,7 @@ findings = [
   "The Rust bridge is the slowest and least reliable step of the payload path, and two measurements say so. One run finished it in 24m21s; the next run log ends at Compiling adreno-metal-bridge with no error line and no Finished banner, which is a process killed rather than a compile failure. Its manifest asks for fat LTO with one codegen unit, the memory-hungry end of cargo, on a three-core hosted runner. Two changes follow: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 for headroom at the cost of wall clock, and an actions cache of build/m2v-target plus build/adreno-metal-bridge keyed by the translator pin file and the recorded patch series, so a second run restores the archive and the plugin skips the build entirely. Both are build-time only; neither changes what the image carries.",
   "The platform seed was validated but never delivered, and the run that first got past the pmgr check measured it: unixnu answered that the platform seed is not stored in any repository, which is scripts/unixnu/payload.py refusing to bake a device tree when the board ADT says unique_chip_id = required. The workflow platform seed step only proved that the repository secret exists and matches eight hex digits. payload.py reads the seed from --unique-chip-id or from UNIXNU_UNIQUE_CHIP_ID, so the job environment now carries that variable from the same secret. The value itself stays out of the repository and out of the record; it is the unit identity that report 2026-11-12 read as cpuid 0x701f5f43, which the workflow check already pinned to the eight-digit form.",
   "The packaging and the record check used the board fork of the tools repository, and both are now pinned to e0ee2ad9 rather than floating its main, because that is the commit the working 191,293,440-byte image of 2026-11-14 was built from; a night of upstream movement can no longer change the build silently. Switching to UniXNU/UniXNU instead was attempted on 2026-11-18 and withdrawn after the first of four independent reviews; the later three reviewed the reduced batch. Three things are measured. First, the catalog: this board selects twenty components (seventeen in [components].include plus QcomGeniSpi, ShengNovatekTouch and VerifiedRoot), UniXNU/UniXNU@bba3b578 defines 28 and misses exactly QcomXnuUsbDebug and Adreno650, while FFT-infra/UniXNU@e0ee2ad9 defines 30 and carries both. Second, a hard blocker in upstream preflight: scripts/unixnu/kernel.py:196-222 at bba3b578, called from cli.py:176-177 on every build kernel, takes a component build command and joins the raw string to the tree, so the QcomXnuUsbDebug row, whose build starts with the component placeholder and /scripts/build.py, resolves to tree/scripts/<placeholder>/ and the first bootstrap build would stop with Build inputs missing before compiling anything. Adreno650 is not part of this blocker: its row names build-adreno650.py, which this repository carries and the tree copies into scripts/. The fork has no preflight, so the switch would introduce the regression. Third, the inputs move: RamBlock revision 4be2d7e to 00a6e5d, the tools checkout drivers/AdrenoMetal gitlink 73d582f to 8c7f950 (the Rust bridge source and its cache key), scripts/data/gpu-metal-vulkan-inputs.json and adreno-compiler-inputs.json, and patches/mesa from 23 to 24 with turnip-darwin-bo-finish-clears-under-lock.patch new, so a build from bba3b578 would not reproduce the 2026-11-14 hashes. The earlier diagnostics finding on this page records the upstream catalog as 25 components; that was a different revision, and the number measured at bba3b578 is 28. Batch two therefore needs both an idempotent catalog supplement (or upstream adding both rows) and placeholder expansion (or a wrapper this repository can carry), plus a kernel-only run before the full image.",
+  "The boot argument table now comes from the upstream tree instead of this fork, and the two are not the same list: five names lost their sheng- prefix in this batch (sheng-vsync to vsync, sheng-gpu-addon to gpu-addon, sheng-fb-bgra to fb-bgra, sheng-fb-gpu to fb-gpu); the sheng-pmgr to pmgr rename already landed with the payload fix, so this batch only adds the reader. sheng-autoreset drops from 600 to 240, and three switches this fork never passed appear: diag=1, log-gpu=1 and metal-archive-fallback=1. The rename is not cosmetic everywhere, and the readers were checked one by one: the pinned base reads gpu-addon (zzy-native-gpu-addon-mount.patch:301) and the board package reads pmgr (ShengPlatformPower.cpp) and fb-gpu (LegacyDisplayProbe.cpp), so two of them really did run under names nothing looked for: gpu-addon, because the fork passed sheng-gpu-addon while the base reads gpu-addon, and pmgr before the payload fix, because the fork passed pmgr while the old ShengPlatformPower read sheng-pmgr. fb-gpu does not belong in that list: the fork passed sheng-fb-gpu and LegacyDisplayProbe read the same name, so for it this is an ordinary rename. vsync, fb-bgra, dpu-scanout, diag, log-gpu and metal-archive-fallback have no reader in either checkout, so for them the table change is forward-looking rather than a fix. configs/prime-list-ios.txt adds the 168 .metallib paths of this board 21H461 image, and configs/wallpaper-bundle/ adds an owner bundle whose Wallpaper.plist declares the @3x logical screen class this device reports.",
 ]
 completion = [
   "All source pins resolve, every selected component has a record, and status shows the intended overrides and patch order.",
@@ -282,6 +283,7 @@ findings = [
   "The GPU client allow-list named PosterBoard, but the processes that run the wallpaper are its extensions: AegirPoster and KaleidoscopePoster abort-looped fifteen and twelve times a boot while PosterBoard itself never appeared. The addon is packed with --clients AegirPoster,KaleidoscopePoster,SpringBoard,iconservicesagent since u260 through scripts/make-gpu-addon-alioth.sh. That is not sufficient on its own: u259 drew with the old list and no poster exits at all, and u261, u262 and u263 all carry the new list and still abort AegirPoster fifteen times and KaleidoscopePoster twelve. The client list decides who may ask, but the data cannot separate it from touch: u259 drew with the old list in a touched boot, and u261 to u263 abort with the new list in untouched ones. A clean comparison needs both lists run untouched. The four slots are all taken by that list, so a fifth process still meets kIOReturnNoSpace.",
   "Measured 2026-10-27 on boot-usb34: the lock screen is stable, SWAP calls=7 ok=7 rej=0, and backboardd creates its resources with kret=0. Earlier builds never submitted a frame at all.",

Then build payload and boot image, verify the payload carries the built kernel, and boot over USB."]
-findings = ["The part answers register reads (ID 0x5652) and returns a CRC-correct all-0xFF buffer while it has no report; an earlier version of FocalTouchProtocol.c treated that buffer as a successful empty frame, which is why every image reported frames=valid with contacts=0.", "Frame reads gated on GPIO 39 going low produced real contacts: at t=100 s two contacts, low count 284, raw 0002805f4598; the part's interrupt counter 0x8F rose from 01 to e0 and its work counter 0x91 advances 60 per second, so the sensor, the SPI link, the CRC and the interrupt line are all working.", "The HID publisher was never in the kernel: ShengHidInput compiles NativeHidInput.cpp but nothing archived it, and an object with no inbound reference is dropped from a plain archive. Selected as a component and archived by the display recipe, as UniXNU-sheng does, it links.", "The official input page describes one merged device -- adapt the descriptor to the sensor, transform coordinates into the display direction, keep ids and count from one frame, publish behind sheng-touch-hid=1 -- and neither reference board splits the digitizer: sheng and pipa both report input as implemented with a single device. Splitting was tried here and left the panel unresponsive with reports=781 and max=5, so sheng-touch-split is commented out in board.toml and should not be re-enabled without evidence the references would support.", "Six defects were found and fixed in one pass, each with a source citation: (1) FocalTouchProtocol.c decoded each axis with shifts of 11 and 3 and took the low bits from PRE[7:5], where the vendor driver (reference/k40-kernel focaltech_core.c:712) uses 12 and 4 from PRE[7:4] and scales by 10/16 -- algebraically the vendor value halved, so every touch landed in the top-left 80 % and the FromEdgeTip band at 97.6 % of the height was unreachable; after the fix a swipe from the bottom reports xy=30479,20319. (2) edge::install returned early once any driver was wrapped, so the second device never had FromEdgeTip injected. (3) The per-contact event field was parsed but never read, so a lift was published as a contact still down (reports fell from 781 to 15 once fixed).
